traceability.notes:
The story `004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS` is fully implemented.
All acceptance criteria are met: - **Core Functionality**: `traceability/require-branch-annotation` detects missing `@story`/`@req` on all defined significant branches (ifs, loops, switch cases, try/catch) and provides targeted auto-fixes with placeholder comments. Unit tests cover all these structures. - **Quality Standards**: Rule follows ESLint best practices (proper meta, schema, configuration validation) and uses efficient helpers. A dedicated performance test ensures it handles large, deeply nested files within a 5-second guardrail. - **Integration**: The rule is wired into the plugin’s recommended/strict presets via `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` and documented as part of the core rules; Jest integration tests for plugin configs also pass. - **User Experience**: Error message `"Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}."` clearly states what is missing (`@story` or `@req`), and auto-fix behavior inserts intuitive placeholder comments at correct locations. - **Error Handling**: Nested branches are handled correctly (inner branches still require their own annotations even when outer ones are annotated), SwitchCase comment association handles blank lines and inline comments, and invalid `branchTypes` configuration is reported with clear messages. - **Documentation**: `user-docs/api-reference.md` contains a dedicated section for `traceability/require-branch-annotation` with description, options, defaults, and a concrete annotated-branch example; the README briefly references the rule and points to user docs.
All technical requirements (REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION, REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING, REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA, REQ-NESTED-HANDLING, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION) are implemented and validated by passing tests. Therefore, this story is assessed as PASSED.
